FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Irdian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Chemical Methods of Test Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division 
Council. 

Testirg of coloured textiles for their resistance to washing, laundering and dry-cleaning is very 
important for their optimum performance durirg everyday use. In order to achieve repeatable 
and reproducible test results, the use of a standard testing apparatus needs no emphasis. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the 
final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for roundirg off numerical values ( revised)'. The number of 
significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified 

in this standard. 



IS 13036 : 1991 

Indian Standard 

TEXTILES - APPARATUS FOR TESTING 

COLOUR FASTNESS OF TEXTILE MATERIALS 

TO WASHING, LAUNDERING AND 

DRY-CLEANING — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes design and con- 
structional requirements of the apparatus for 
testing colour fastness of textile materials 
to washing, laundering and dry-cleaning. 

2 REFERENCES 

2.1 The Indian Standards given in Annex A are 
necessary adjuncts to this standard. 

3 DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTIONAL 
REQUIREMENTS 

3.1 The apparatus shall consist of: 

a) glass or stainless steel containers in which 
the test specimens or composite speci- 
mens, test solution and stainless steel 
balls or stainless steel discs are to be 
contained together, 

b) a device to revolve the containers, and 

c) a theromostatic water bath to maintain 
the temperature of test solution in the 
containers at a constant value as required 
in the test. 

An illustrative diagram of the apparatus is 
shown in Fig, L 

3.2 Glass or Stainless Steel Containers 

The containers shall be made either from glass 
conforming to the relevant requirements given 



in IS 2619 : 1971 or from stainless steel con- 
forming to IS 5522 : 1978, leak proofed and 
sealed. They shall be of 75 ± 5 mm diameter, 
125 ± 10 mm height and 550 ± 50 ml capacity. 
They shall be able to withstand a revolving speed 
of 40 ± 2 rev/min without any damage. They 
shall have smooth surface and shall be free 
from rough edges. 

NOTE — The containers should preferably be 
cylindrical in shape. 

3.3 Revolving Device 

It shall consist of an electric motor, a revolving 
shaft and holders for containers fixed to the 
revolving shaft radially. It shall enable the 
containers to be fixed so that the centre line of 
holders may position in one line with the centre 
line of the containers. It shall be capable of 
rotating the shaft/container assembly at a speed 
of 40 ± 2 rev/min. The distance between* the 
centre line of the revolving shaft and the bottom 
of the containers shall be 45 ± 10 mm. 

3.4 Thermostatic Water Bath 

It shall be provided with a heater capable of 
keeping the temperature of the test solution 
contained in the rotating containers at the 
specified temperature within ± 2°C. 

3.5 Stainless Steel Balls 

They shall be non-corrodible, made from 
stainless steel conforming to IS 6603 : 1972 and 
shall have a diameter of 6 ± 0'4 mm.

IS 13036 : 1991 

NOTE — The stainless steel balls shall be used for 
severe washing and laundering tests as prescribed 
in IS 765 : 1079 and IS 3417 : 1979. For dry- 
cleaning test given in IS 4802 : 1988, stainless steel 
discs, as prescribed in 3.6, shall be used. 

3.6 Stainless Steel Discs 

They shall be non-corrodible, made from stainless 
steel conforming to IS 6603 : 1972 and shall have 
a diameter of 30 ± 2 mm and mass of 20 ± 2 g. 
They shall be smooth and free from rough 
edges. 

4 INSPECTION AND TESTING 

4.1 The apparatus shall be checked for the 
requirements specified in 3.1 to 3.6 and the 
following: 

a) All containers, holders, thermostatic water 
bath and stainless steel discs shall be 
checked for defects like pin holes, cavities, 
etc, 

b) The entire apparatus shall be checked for 
static and dynamic balancing for smooth 
working and any unbalance shall be 
removed; 

c) The electric circuit shall be checked to 
avoid any short circuiting in operation; 

d) The temperature control mechanism shall 
be checked for its proper working and 



the instrument shall be calibrated to read 
accurate temperature; and 

e) The revolving device shall be checked for 
proper working and periodic calibration 
of speed, preferably by speed indicator, 
shall be done. 

5 PACKING 

5.1 The entire apparatus assembly shall be 
packed with strong and sturdy packing so as to 
avoid damage during transit. 

6 MARKING 

6.1 The apparatus shall be marked at appro- 
priate place with the following: 

a) The name of the apparatus, 

b) Indication of the source of manufacture, 
and 

c) The month and year of manufacture of 
the apparatus. 

6.2 The apparatus may also be marked with the 
Standard Mark. 

7 CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

7.1 The apparatus shall be declared as conform- 
ing to the requirements of this standard if it 
satisfies all the requirements given in this 
standard.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to 
that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards, 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of 
goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications^ No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in 
the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or 
grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publication ), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards

are issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in
